newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine union head says will continue in post.
newsitem.headline: Argentine union head says will continue in post.

text.p: The head of Argentina's main labour union federation, the CGT, on Wednesday denied that he is about to resign and said he is open to a new dialogue with the government.
Rodolfo Daer, the CGT chief, told state news agency Telam: "I am prepared to have a dialogue with the government, but without it meaning a diminution of workers' dignity."

The comments came after the CGT staged a 24-hour general strike on December 26 -- the third last year -- protesting President Carlos Menem's decision to sign three decrees on labour market reforms which the unions fear will reduce their powers. The president made the decision of decreeing the proposals after talks with the CGT broke down.
On Tuesday Menem's cabinet chief, Jorge Rodriguez, said he had had initial talks with CGT leaders to restart the dialogue with the unions.
Separately, Daer told Telam: "I am not thinking of resigning."

Local media have said rifts are opening up within Argentina's labour movement with some arguing for harder measures to fight Menem's free market reforms than the strikes that have been staged by the CGT.
For instance, the MTA union has threatened to walk out of the CGT unless it puts into action a policy of tougher confrontation with the government.
The MTA staged a protest against hunger and unemployment during the traditional New Year festivities outside the government Casa Rosada building.
